$meta.role: The register of design and implementation decisions Phase 1 cannot make on its own. Every decision id cited anywhere in design-manifest.json or the token generator must appear here, and a test enforces that.
$meta.rule: An entry is closed only by the named owner. Nothing here may be resolved by choosing a value in code — that is a design change, and AC13 fails any element with no design source. Statuses are 'open' until the owner rules.

decisions.title: Compact row height — 28px or 26px
decisions.phase1Impact: Blocks the token row.compact. No Phase 1 component consumes it; SyCollection's density modes will.
decisions.statement: Foundations §15 states 28px. The Design System's density prop states 26px. Both documents are canonical and the handoff records the disagreement as conflict C1 without resolving it — the design's only self-declared blocking conflict.
decisions.evidence: design-tokens.json row.compact carries the conflict inline as its value.

decisions.title: Tokenise the focus ring (audit F9)
decisions.phase1Impact: Blocks the token focus.ring. base.css still implements the rule, from --color-accent-default plus the two 2px figures §16 states verbatim, because §16 says the ring is never removed.
decisions.statement: Foundations §16 states 'a 2px accent ring with a 2px offset on every focusable element, never removed', and §10.11 names accent.default as the ring colour — but no focus.ring.{color,width,offset} trio exists. Audit finding F9 records the omission. Minting the trio was proposed and stood down pending the design owner's ruling; it is neither adopted nor rejected.
decisions.evidence: design-tokens.json focus.ring has the value 'UNSPECIFIED BY DESIGN'. design-decisions.json is empty and wired, so an approved trio drops straight in.
decisions.mustNotDo: Emit focus.ring tokens, or treat the stand-down as a permanent rejection.

decisions.title: Which icon set
decisions.phase1Impact: No Phase 1 token or component. Blocks Slice 6's Icon primitive.
decisions.statement: Foundations §15 specifies the geometry — stroke-based, 16px in dense contexts, 20px in toolbars, on a 24px grid with 1.5px strokes — but never names the set. The sizing tokens for all four figures are implemented; only the glyph source is undecided.
decisions.evidence: design-tokens.json icon.dense / icon.toolbar / icon.grid / icon.stroke are implemented; no token names a family.
decisions.mustNotDo: Adopt an icon library because its geometry happens to match.

decisions.title: ease.standard and ease.exit are not valid CSS
decisions.phase1Impact: Blocks both easing tokens. No Phase 1 component animates, so nothing is waiting on them.
decisions.statement: Foundations §13's motion table declares ease.standard as 'cubic(.2,0,0,1)' and ease.exit as 'cubic(.4,0,1,1)'. cubic() is not a CSS function; cubic-bezier() is, and takes exactly the four control points stated. Expanding the notation would preserve every number and invent none — but it is still an interpretation of a malformed value, so it waits on the design owner.
decisions.evidence: Verified against the source document, not only the handoff: Foundations v0.2's own motion array literally contains dur: "cubic(.2,0,0,1)". The handoff and the inventory transcribed it faithfully — the defect is in the canonical source, and the generator's duration validator is what surfaced it.
decisions.discovered: Phase 1, Slice 3. Not anticipated by the Phase 1 plan, which counted 2 blocked tokens by scanning for UNSPECIFIED BY DESIGN and the C1 conflict marker — neither of which flags a value that merely looks well-formed.
decisions.mustNotDo: Emit cubic-bezier() without the owner confirming the notation was the intent.

decisions.title: Three contrast pairings below the floor §16 commits to
decisions.phase1Impact: None blocked. All three token values are implemented unchanged and pinned by the AC3 contrast matrix as documented gaps rather than regressions.
decisions.statement: Foundations §16 makes AA the floor and requires 3:1 for non-text affordances. Three pairings computed from the frozen token values do not meet it. The values are left exactly as the design states them.

pairings.measured: 1.39–1.56:1 light, 1.61–2.12:1 dark, across all four surfaces
pairings.designClaim: §16 claims 3:1 for non-text affordances only via icon.subtle. border.strong is never claimed — but §10.1 names it for 'input borders, focusable edges', which is exactly what 1.4.11 covers.
pairings.question: Is the low contrast deliberate, or does border.strong need a darker value?

pairings.designClaim: §10.1 states 4.6:1, and §16 insists 'a disabled control that cannot be read is not a state, it is a defect'. The stated figure does not match the values: they give 4.47.
pairings.question: Was 4.6:1 the target, in which case one of the two values needs adjusting?

pairings.designClaim: §10.1 claims text.tertiary 'passes AA on every ground in the system'. True in light — worst case 4.75 — but false on the dark selected surface. Consistent with audit F10: no component or screen has ever been drawn in dark.
pairings.question: Does the dark palette need revisiting, or is the claim scoped to light only?

decisions.evidence: src/contrast.test.ts computes all 60 pairings and pins these as documented gaps. A new failure is reported separately, as a regression.
decisions.mustNotDo: Change a token value to make the matrix pass.

decisions.title: No foreground token for a filled ground
decisions.phase1Impact: Blocks nothing. SyButton's primary variant paints its label with surface.default, which is the value the canonical screen draws.
decisions.statement: The design carries three text tokens — text.primary, text.secondary, text.tertiary — all dark-on-light in the light theme, and none intended to sit on a filled accent or status ground. A filled primary button therefore has no token for its own label. §10.1 names accent.default as "Primary action" but stops at the fill.
decisions.evidence: The canonical Vocabulary screen paints the primary action "New sign" as background #2f6b52 with color #ffffff. #2f6b52 is accent.default and #ffffff is exactly surface.default's light value, so surface.default is used as the foreground rather than a new token being minted (AC13). It behaves correctly in dark too, where both sides flip: surface.default #1f2124 on accent.default #6ab894. Both pairings are already in the AC3 matrix and clear AA — 6.28:1 light, 6.84:1 dark.
decisions.discovered: Phase 1, Slice 6, while implementing SyButton's primary variant.
decisions.question: Should a text.on-accent (or similar) token exist, or is reusing surface.default as the figure on a filled ground the intended reading?
decisions.mustNotDo: Mint a foreground token, or hardcode #ffffff in a component.
